title: 28 U.S.C. § 1391 — venue
summary: Venue identifies the geographically proper court within the relevant court system. It allocates the location of litigation and is distinct from subject-matter jurisdiction and personal jurisdiction.

sections.Role in the course: Venue identifies the geographically proper court within the relevant court system. It allocates the location of litigation and is distinct from subject-matter jurisdiction and personal jurisdiction.
sections.What to examine: Read the applicable venue statute, identify the defendants’ relevant residences and where substantial events or property are located, and determine whether a general or special provision governs. Bates illustrates why an event’s receipt in a district can matter.
